diff --git a/src/services/notify-service.research.test.ts b/src/services/notify-service.research.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..a3343eb932e7d8d8884880612cf6e12b5c067c8f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/services/notify-service.research.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+import { EAST_CHANNEL, WEST_CHANNEL } from '../../test/support/gyms.js';
+import { dmBrief, dmReasons, dmSentence, linksOf } from '../../test/support/messages.js';
+import { ALICE, BOB, CAROL, REPORTER } from '../../test/support/parties.js';
+import { partyServiceWith } from '../../test/support/party-service.js';
+import { pageTask, researchTasksOfPage } from '../../test/support/research.js';
+import { reportedStop } from '../../test/support/stop-report-cases.js';
+import { MemoryStopReports } from '../../test/support/stop-reports.js';
+import { INTO_THE_WILD } from '../../test/support/research-store-cases.js';
+import type { ResearchEvent } from '../domain/time/research-events.js';
+import { DateTime } from 'luxon';
+import { watchEachTest } from '../../test/support/timers.js';
+import { boxTarget, type TargetWant } from '../domain/notify/target-wants.js';
+import type { ResearchTask } from '../domain/research/task.js';
+import type { ReportedStop } from '../domain/stops/report.js';
+import { postLink } from '../render/notify-dm.js';
+import type { NotifyServiceOptions } from './notify-service.js';
+import { DM_PRIORITY } from './dm-sender.js';
+import { StopReportService } from './stop-reports.js';
+
+const background = watchEachTest();
+const at = (local: string): number =>
+  DateTime.fromISO(local, { zone: 'America/New_York' }).toMillis();
+
+const DRAGON = pageTask('Catch a Dragon-type Pokémon');
+const RESEARCH_DRATINI = boxTarget('research-pokemon', 147);
+const RITA = { id: REPORTER, name: 'Rita' };
+
+/** Stops in West (40.0–40.1, −80.1–−80.0) and one in East. */
+const west = (n: number): ReportedStop => reportedStop(n, { lat: 40.05 + n / 1_000, lon: -80.05 });
+const east = reportedStop(90, { lat: 40.05, lon: -79.95 });
+
+/** A task of the page that gives this reward. */
+function taskGiving(fits: (reward: ResearchTask['rewards'][number]) => boolean): ResearchTask {
+  const found = researchTasksOfPage().find((task) => task.rewards.some(fits));
+  if (!found) throw new Error('the page has no such task');
+  return found;
+}
+
+/** The notifier of the party tests, told of the research reports of a report service. */
+async function researchWith(
+  notifying: Partial<NotifyServiceOptions> = {},
+  events: ResearchEvent[] = [],
+) {
+  const made = await partyServiceWith([], { notifying });
+  const reports = new StopReportService({
+    store: new MemoryStopReports(),
+    events: { researchEvents: () => events },
+    zone: made.settings.timezone,
+    log: made.log,
+    now: () => made.clock.now,
+  });
+  reports.listen({ reported: (news) => made.notify.researchReported(news) });
+  const want = (memberId: string, ...targets: TargetWant[]) =>
+    made.targetWants.change(memberId, made.gateway.guildId, { add: targets, remove: [] }, 0);
+  const report = async (
+    task: ResearchTask,
+    stops: ReportedStop[],
+    reporter: { id: string; name: string } = RITA,
+  ) => {
+    const outcome = await reports.reportResearch({
+      serverId: made.gateway.guildId,
+      stops,
+      subject: {
+        subjectKey: task.key,
+        research: { text: task.text, category: task.category, rewards: task.rewards, typed: false },
+      },
+      reporter,
+    });
+    await made.notify.flush();
+    return outcome;
+  };
+  return { ...made, reports, want, report };
+}
+
+describe('NotifyService: field research is reported (plan 8R-1, design 7)', () => {
+  it('tells who wants a reward of the task, once, naming every stop of the report', async () => {
+    const made = await researchWith();
+    await made.want(ALICE, RESEARCH_DRATINI);
+    // A raid want of Dratini, or another reward, is no research want.
+    await made.want(BOB, boxTarget('research-pokemon', 1));
+    await made.wants.set(CAROL, made.gateway.guildId, { kind: 'pokemon', dex: 147 }, 'both');
+    // The reporter knows.
+    await made.want(REPORTER, RESEARCH_DRATINI);
+    await made.report(DRAGON, [west(1), west(2)]);
+    expect(made.dms.recipients).toEqual([ALICE]);
+    const [message] = made.dms.to(ALICE);
+    expect(dmSentence(message)).toBe(
+      `Field research has been reported in <#${WEST_CHANNEL}> by **Rita**: ` +
+        '**Catch a Dragon-type Pokémon**.',
+    );
+    expect(dmBrief(message)).toEqual([
+      '**Rewards** one of Dratini, Bagon, Axew +4',
+      '- **Yellow Mural 1** · Market Street',
+      '- **Yellow Mural 2** · Market Street',
+      'Until midnight.',
+    ]);
+    expect(dmReasons(message)).toEqual(['Dratini (research)']);
+    // In rehearsal mode (no posts) the DM has no link.
+    expect(linksOf(message)).toEqual([]);
+    expect(made.dms.jobs[0]).toEqual(
+      expect.objectContaining({
+        priority: DM_PRIORITY.normal,
+        expiresAt: expect.any(Number) as number,
+      }),
+    );
+  });
+
+  it('links to the message of the post that holds the task', async () => {
+    const asked: string[] = [];
+    const made = await researchWith({
+      researchPosts: {
+        messageOf: (channelId, subjectKey) => {
+          asked.push(`${channelId} ${subjectKey}`);
+          return Promise.resolve('300000000000000077');
+        },
+      },
+    });
+    await made.want(ALICE, RESEARCH_DRATINI);
+    await made.report(DRAGON, [west(1)]);
+    expect(asked).toEqual([`${WEST_CHANNEL} ${DRAGON.key}`]);
+    expect(linksOf(made.dms.to(ALICE)[0])).toEqual([
+      `Go to post ${postLink(made.gateway.guildId, WEST_CHANNEL, '300000000000000077')}`,
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('names only the new stops when the task is reported at more, never a stop twice', async () => {
+    const made = await researchWith();
+    await made.want(ALICE, RESEARCH_DRATINI);
+    const first = await made.report(DRAGON, [west(1)]);
+    await made.report(DRAGON, [west(2), west(1)], { id: BOB, name: 'Bob' });
+    expect(made.dms.to(ALICE).map((message) => dmBrief(message).slice(1, -1))).toEqual([
+      ['- **Yellow Mural 1** · Market Street'],
+      ['- **Yellow Mural 2** · Market Street'],
+    ]);
+    // Taken back and reported again in the period: no news for who was told.
+    const id = first.saved[0]?.report.id ?? 0;
+    await made.reports.takeBack(made.gateway.guildId, [id], REPORTER, false);
+    await made.report(DRAGON, [west(1)]);
+    expect(made.dms.to(ALICE)).toHaveLength(2);
+  });
+
+  it('tells only who can view the region channel, one DM per region', async () => {
+    const made = await researchWith();
+    await made.want(ALICE, RESEARCH_DRATINI);
+    await made.want(BOB, RESEARCH_DRATINI);
+    made.gateway.shutOut(EAST_CHANNEL, BOB);
+    await made.report(DRAGON, [west(1), east]);
+    expect(made.dms.to(ALICE).map(dmSentence)).toEqual([
+      expect.stringContaining(`<#${WEST_CHANNEL}>`),
+      expect.stringContaining(`<#${EAST_CHANNEL}>`),
+    ]);
+    expect(made.dms.to(BOB).map(dmSentence)).toEqual([
+      expect.stringContaining(`<#${WEST_CHANNEL}>`),
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('tells who wants an item or Mega Energy the task gives', async () => {
+    const made = await researchWith();
+    const candy = taskGiving((reward) => reward.kind === 'item' && reward.item === 'rare-candy');
+    const energy = taskGiving((reward) => reward.kind === 'energy');
+    const energyDex = energy.rewards.find((reward) => reward.kind === 'energy')?.dex ?? 0;
+    await made.want(ALICE, { kind: 'research-item', item: 'rare-candy' });
+    await made.want(BOB, { kind: 'research-energy', dex: energyDex });
+    await made.report(candy, [west(1)]);
+    await made.report(energy, [west(2)]);
+    expect(made.dms.to(ALICE).map(dmReasons)).toEqual([['Rare Candy (research)']]);
+    expect(made.dms.to(BOB)).toHaveLength(1);
+  });
+
+  it('says until when a multi-day event’s day and its last day hold (B7)', async () => {
+    const made = await researchWith({}, [INTO_THE_WILD]);
+    await made.want(ALICE, RESEARCH_DRATINI);
+    made.clock.now = at('2026-11-10T12:00');
+    await made.report(DRAGON, [west(1)]);
+    made.clock.now = at('2026-11-13T12:00');
+    await made.report(DRAGON, [west(1)]);

### Task 9: 8R-1 docs: reports at stops, the want dialog, Pine stops, guides

Prototype commit: `4321ab48a16e893c8f28ac15b8639affa2ba38cd`

A new area file docs/architecture/stop-reports.md (the tables of migration
026, stops of Pine's own and /pokestop, the task list, research periods,
the stop reports and /research, the pinned post "Today at the stops", the
research DMs). notifications-and-dms.md: TargetWant, /want's dialog of
boxes, max battles by the Dynamax and Gigantamax boxes, researchReported,
the Stop buttons' new arguments. wayfarer.md and gyms-and-regions.md: Pine
stops in WayspotDirectory and PlaceFinder, the import preview's line.
discord-framework.md: a control counting in a command's varied window
whose throttle is a function of the settings. testing.md: the helpers and
fakes of 8R-1.

The max-battles design's decision 6 and section 3.4 point to the stop
reports design; step 18 of the 8X-3 staging ticks the Dynamax and
Gigantamax boxes. The guides name /research and /pokestop, the research
settings and the optional Pin Messages (the invite's permissions number);
the official announcement draft names field research. Follow-ups: what to
watch on Leek Duck's page on 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-21, and the open items
of the prototype.

diff --git a/docs/architecture/discord-framework.md b/docs/architecture/discord-framework.md
index 012d881032da021b0b0e50ae6e559e74bd130034..bd7e3549e8ab259592535da7688f874196f80405 100644
--- a/docs/architecture/discord-framework.md
+++ b/docs/architecture/discord-framework.md
@@ -24,7 +24,7 @@ How the bot talks to Discord apart from parties: slash commands and their router
 
 - Controls are `ComponentHandler`s listed in `src/components/index.ts`, one per custom-id kind, with a function per control type (`button`, `select`, `modal`). A command's guards do not cover its controls: give the handler its own `guards`. Its `throttle` may be a function of the interaction and the custom id (asked after the guards; undefined lets a control through uncounted): `/counters` counts a submitted dialog in the command's window and the button that opens it in a `MEMBER_READ_THROTTLE` window of its own. A limit with `as` (`ControlThrottle`) counts in the window of that command, as the router counts the command's uses (the dialog of `/counters` runs the command's work against Pokebattler: command and submits share its three a minute, "You can use /counters again in …"); without it a control counts in its kind's own window (`controlThrottleKey(kind)`, `component:<kind>`), as `/rank`'s and `/help`'s do. The bot gives the router its `Throttles` (`RouterOptions.throttles`) and shares them with the web server, whose presses of a party's buttons count in the window of the post's controls (plan 8M-3). What a control refuses belongs in a guard of its handler, which runs before the throttle, so that a refusal does not count (`requireDialogPlan` of `/counters`' dialog).
 - A dialog (a modal; `showModal`, the first answer: nothing is deferred before it) holds up to five labels, rows of a text input and text displays. Checked on the test server (2026-10-18, plan 8T-H): a dialog of one text display alone opens and submits (the split's one-group dialog), and a label may hold a radio group (`ComponentType.RadioGroup`, 2 to 10 choices of a label, value and description of 100 each), read with `fields.getRadioGroup(id, true)`; a required one cannot be submitted empty (Discord refuses Submit), so nothing is preselected where a pick must be deliberate. Labels and descriptions of choices are assumed to show no markdown, as those of select menus do (not yet checked on Discord: 8T staging step 28 checks it): they carry the members' text as it is, not `plain()`.
-- A question asked once ("Remove all your wants?", "Close this raid?", the split of a train; plans 8T-H, 8Q, design `2026-10-18-one-shot-dialogs-design.md`) is a dialog, not a private reply with buttons: it opens over the channel at once and closes when answered. They are Remove all of the wants and gym targets (`notifications-and-dms.md`), staff's `/delete` and Close…, Refuse place…, Block maker… of a report's post (`removalDialog`, `moderation.md`), deleting a gym and `/region remove` (`gyms-and-regions.md`), `/location` to another region (`parties-and-posts.md`), the split of a train (`trains.md`) and `/max`'s question about a battle that ends soon (plan 8X-3, `parties-and-posts.md`: no read from the database, the slow-read rule's clock checked before it opens; its Submit `max:<token>:report`, a pending-request token, carries on the use `/max` counted); the panels used again and again, the import previews and the like stay private replies. The pieces are `src/discord/dialog.ts`: `dialog({ customId, title, text?, choice?, field? })` (the title says the act, cut to 45 characters; the text is the question, ending with what Submit does when there is no choice, `Submit removes them.`, and may be left out of a dialog that is its choice alone; a choice between ways is a required radio group with nothing picked, so that Submit never does the harsher one by default, read at Submit with `pickedOf` (undefined for a Submit without that group, a dialog of an older shape or a forged one: the handler then answers stale); when only one way is possible there is no choice and the text says why). Plan 8X-1B: a choice may name the value `picked` to start with (Discord's `default`; the fakes refuse two, as Discord would), which goes first in its list where the order allows: Android picks a radio group's first choice by itself whatever is marked (Matt's check, 2026-10-20), an iPhone only what is marked, so a choice that must not be made by accident is never first; `menu: true` makes it a string select of up to 25 for a longer list (Meet…, `getStringSelectValues`), whose default is marked only (it keeps its order); `field` is one optional line of text (`TextInputStyle.Short`, `required: false`). A command whose throttle varies counts in `variedThrottleKey(name, limit)`; a control that counts in that window (`as`, Meet…'s dialog in `/meet`'s) is refused in the command's words, the name before the line break ("You can use /meet again in …"). Discord's Cancel replaces the Keep and Cancel buttons: it closes the dialog and nothing is said. **The slow-read rule:** what a dialog needs from the database (a count, a report, a gym's references, the member's privacy) is read through `readInTime(log, interaction, work)`, within `DIALOG_READ_MS` (2 seconds, of Discord's 3) of when the interaction was made (its `createdTimestamp`, as the late deferral counts): past it no dialog opens and the member is told privately `SLOW_READ` ("That took me too long to look up: try again in a moment."), a `UserError` that gives the use back; a refusal of the read itself passes on (also one thrown at once, which leaves no timer), a read that comes back past the budget by the clock is refused too (also before its timer ran, on a busy event loop), and a read that fails after it was given up is logged. A command that opens a dialog declares no `defer`, and a control does not defer before it. The dialog carries what it needs in its custom id (the party, the gym, the region, the report); a pending-request token only where a value does not fit or must not be shown. Its Submit is a `modal` of the handler of the same kind, with the same guards and throttle as the press it replaces (opening counts as the question did); it is acknowledged privately at once (`deferSubmit`), decides everything again, and answers privately (`editReply`, `answerApart`, or a `UserError` the router says). **Channels in a dialog are named, not mentioned:** `channelInDialog(name)` (`#oakland`; `a deleted channel` for one the bot cannot find), since whether Discord shows `<#id>` inside a dialog is not checked yet (8Q staging); the answers after Submit keep their mentions. Tests read a dialog with `test/support/dialogs.ts`.

 - A press on the controls of an answer (plan 8B-2) is answered through `pressAnswer` / `deferPress` / `answerPress` (`src/discord/late-reply.ts`): on a public answer (`/rank`, `/counters` in a post) the member who asked (`message.interactionMetadata.user`, never the deprecated `interaction`) changes the answer for everybody (`update`), anybody else gets a private copy with the change; a press on a private answer always changes it; `onlyPrivate` (a Pokébox) gives even the asker a copy. Work that takes time acknowledges first as it will answer (`deferUpdate` or a private `deferReply`; a form submitted from no message has nothing to update and is deferred as a copy). A public answer in a party's post whose party has ended is never edited: the press answers privately.
 - A control that answers in the place of the message it is on, where that message may be from before it was v2, uses `showInPlace(press, message, oldLine?)` and `sayInPlace(press, text, accent)` (`src/discord/late-reply.ts`; `onV2Message`): on a v2 message an `update` (or an edit after `deferUpdate`) with its files replacing the old ones (`attachments: []`); on a classic one `sayInPlace` answers plain text, and `showInPlace` closes it with `oldLine` (`ANSWERED_BELOW` unless given) and sends the v2 message as a private follow-up, since whether Discord takes a v2 interaction update of a classic message is not known and is not tried; a form a command opened is answered privately. Controls backed by `PendingRequests` (the questions of `/gym` and `/region`) meet a message from before a restart as expired, so these classic paths are a safety net for them; in practice only stateless controls (the `/iam` menus) reach them. An answer in a private message of its own (a command, or a press acknowledged with `deferReply`: `answeredApart`, told by discord.js setting `ephemeral` for a reply or `deferReply` and not for `update` or `deferUpdate`) goes through `answerApart(interaction, message)`; `showInPlace` throws there, and `sayInPlace` answers apart. In tests the fake controls take `v2Message: true` for a press on a v2 message whose rows the test does not give (`gymCommandsWith` and `regionCommandsWith` press so by default; `v2Message: false` is a message from before), and refuse as Discord would: a v2 `update` (or edit after `deferUpdate`) of a classic message ("a classic-to-v2 update is not tried"), a v2 message made classic, and a file component, thumbnail or gallery picture naming a file the message does not carry (a reply and a follow-up carry only their own `files`; an edit that sends `files` without `attachments` keeps none of the old ones, as discord.js sends it). `V2Message.files` are `MessageFile`s: a local path, or text made with its name (`{ attachment: Buffer, name }`).

 - Gyms are found through `ctx.gyms` (`search(channelId, text, { limit })`, `get`, `isRegion`, `regionsOf`, `inRegion`): all gyms are held in memory by `GymDirectory`. A hit says where it lies (`place`: `local`, `neighbouring`, `anywhere`), whether every word matched (`allWords`; false means a guess), whether a word had to be read as a misspelling (`corrected`) and how far the reading is (`typos`, `typoCost` of `src/domain/search/text.ts`: per typed word nothing as typed, a quarter for a word it only begins, else the fewest wrong letters, read by the words found in the gym's name, nickname or keywords, a word found only in its places, description or address costing 3: `namedReading`; a stop's or power spot's by its title, its street counting so): corrected matches and guesses come by how many typed words they lack (`missed` of `reading`: a guess that found more of the words first, whatever its misspellings), then by it, then by score (plan 8W-3: the score weighs a rare word high, so "libary" read as "Vicary" with two letters wrong came before the libraries with one). Act only on a clear hit; offer the rest as a choice. After a gym edit call `GymDirectory.refreshGym(id)`; after regions change, `load()`.
 - `ctx.regions` (`RegionDirectory`) has the regions by id, channel and forum; `GymDirectory` holds its own copy, so after a region changes load both. Every change to what either directory holds bumps its `generation` (`GymDirectory`: every load, gym re-read or forgotten; `RegionDirectory`: every load): the web map's cache (`GeoCache`, `web.md`) rebuilds a server's view only when a generation differs, so a new way of changing either directory's state must bump it too, or the map keeps showing the old state. `regionChannelOf` also answers for a region's forum and a post in it. `ctx.users.get(snowflake)` gives a member's settings.
-- Gyms, PokéStops and power spots together are found through `ctx.placeFinder` (`PlaceFinder`, `src/services/place-finder.ts`; plan 8W-2, Matt's rules of 2026-10-15): the server's gyms through the gym search (`GymLookupOptions.within`, the gyms of its regions: a gym elsewhere with every word leaves the server's guesses alone; `PlaceFinder` takes what it needs of `GymDirectory` by `Pick`, and `GymProvider` has no `all()`), the stops and power spots each through a `WayspotIndex` of their own (`src/domain/search/wayspot-index.ts`: title, and counting little the street and town; every word as typed or as a beginning; one letter wrong only when nothing matched as typed, or when a word as typed looks misspelt (a word one letter off is in at least `MISSPELT_TITLES` 3 titles and three times as many as it: "Little Free Libary" beside the libraries, plan 8W-3), whose corrections then follow its hits as typed; guesses by some words only when nothing else matched; common words weigh little by MiniSearch's BM25, the legacy stop words not at all), never one mixed index; merged by `mergePlaces` (`place-merge.ts`: `placeFit` exact, word, beginning, loose, guess, the guesses by `guessRank` across kinds (fewer typed words missed first, then the fewest letters read wrong); then the member's region; then gym, stop, power spot; then fewer title words beyond those typed, `extraWords`, counted in the name the fit came from (`placeFitBy`: a gym's name or nickname), tuned on Pittsburgh's export; then score). Only what lies in a region of the server is found (`find`, `chosen(value)`); a choice says where it is (`where`: its street, or "near <gym>", the nearest of the server's gyms within `NEAR_GYM_METRES` 1 km, never the place itself; with none so near, nothing); a value is `<kind>:<id>` (`placeValue`, `readPlaceValue`); typed text is acted on only through `clearOf(found)`, of the list one `find` gave (`clearPlace`: the one hit, of every kind and region, whose every word matched exactly, `exact` or `word`; one that names it outright beside another with every word is no clear hit). The indexes are built after every change of what the Wayspots are (`ctx.wayspots.contentGeneration`, told by `whenChanged`: a load; not a change of the regions, nor a forget: a forgotten Wayspot is passed over at once because the search takes only what `inRegion` has) in a turn of their own (`setImmediate`, about half a second for a city), never inside a search: a search before the first build finds the gyms alone, one after a load what was built until the new build is done; `built()` waits for a build that is due (tests).
+- Gyms, PokéStops and power spots together are found through `ctx.placeFinder` (`PlaceFinder`, `src/services/place-finder.ts`; plan 8W-2, Matt's rules of 2026-10-15): the server's gyms through the gym search (`GymLookupOptions.within`, the gyms of its regions: a gym elsewhere with every word leaves the server's guesses alone; `PlaceFinder` takes what it needs of `GymDirectory` by `Pick`, and `GymProvider` has no `all()`), the stops (the kept Wayspots and, plan 8R-1, the stops of Pine's own that staff add with `/pokestop`, `stop-reports.md`) and power spots each through a `WayspotIndex` of their own (`src/domain/search/wayspot-index.ts`: title, and counting little the street and town; every word as typed or as a beginning; one letter wrong only when nothing matched as typed, or when a word as typed looks misspelt (a word one letter off is in at least `MISSPELT_TITLES` 3 titles and three times as many as it: "Little Free Libary" beside the libraries, plan 8W-3), whose corrections then follow its hits as typed; guesses by some words only when nothing else matched; common words weigh little by MiniSearch's BM25, the legacy stop words not at all), never one mixed index; merged by `mergePlaces` (`place-merge.ts`: `placeFit` exact, word, beginning, loose, guess, the guesses by `guessRank` across kinds (fewer typed words missed first, then the fewest letters read wrong); then the member's region; then gym, stop, power spot; then fewer title words beyond those typed, `extraWords`, counted in the name the fit came from (`placeFitBy`: a gym's name or nickname), tuned on Pittsburgh's export; then score). The indexes are built after every change of what the Wayspots are (`ctx.wayspots.contentGeneration`, told by `whenChanged`: a load; not a change of the regions, nor a forget: a forgotten Wayspot is passed over at once because the search takes only what `inRegion` has) in a turn of their own (`setImmediate`, about half a second for a city), never inside a search: a search before the first build finds the gyms alone, one after a load what was built until the new build is done; `built()` waits for a build that is due (tests).

 # Notifications and direct messages
 
-What members ask to be told about (wants, gym targets, new trains, boss-set), how the notifier matches a change of a party against it, how direct messages are queued and sent, the DMs themselves with their Stop buttons, and spawn reports with Unown sightings. Read before changing wants, gym targets, the notifier, DMs or `/wild`.
+What members ask to be told about (wants and `/want`'s boxes, gym targets, new trains, boss-set), how the notifier matches a change of a party against it, how direct messages are queued and sent, the DMs themselves with their Stop buttons, and spawn reports with Unown sightings. Read before changing wants, gym targets, the notifier, DMs or `/wild`.
 
 ## Wants and gym targets
 
-- A want (`PokemonNotification`) is per member and server and is one of: a species (every form, megas included), one form (`form`, a catalogue key), the shadow raids of either (`shadow`; raids only), a raid tier (raids only), perfect or zero IVs (spawns only); a mega is raids only. The columns are read and written only through the codec (`notification-target.ts`: `readNotification` gives the target and the scope in effect; a row it cannot read is skipped, counted and never deleted on its own) and the pure functions of `src/domain/pogo/wants.ts` (`readWants`, `planSetWant`, `rowsOfWant`: duplicate legacy rows are one want with the union of their scopes, two keys of one catalogue entry are one want, a row is rewritten only when its meaning changes). `ctx.wants` (`WantStorage`: `list`, `set`, `remove`, `removeAll`, `count`) is the repository; `MemoryWants` (`test/support/wants.ts`) is its twin and runs the same functions. `pokemonWantFits(catalogue, target, entry, shadowRaid)` says whether a want is for a boss or a spawn.
+- A want (`PokemonNotification`) is per member and server and is one of: a species (every form, megas included), one form (`form`, a catalogue key), the shadow raids of either (`shadow`; raids only), a raid tier (raids only), perfect or zero IVs (spawns only); a mega is raids only. The columns are read and written only through the codec (`notification-target.ts`: `readNotification` gives the target and the scope in effect; a row it cannot read is skipped, counted and never deleted on its own) and the pure functions of `src/domain/pogo/wants.ts` (`readWants`, `planSetWant`, `rowsOfWant`: duplicate legacy rows are one want with the union of their scopes, two keys of one catalogue entry are one want, a row is rewritten only when its meaning changes). `ctx.wants` (`WantStorage`: `list`, `set`, `remove`, `removeAll`, `count`) is the repository; `MemoryWants` (`test/support/wants.ts`) is its twin and runs the same functions. `pokemonWantFits(catalogue, target, entry, shadowRaid)` says whether a want is for a boss or a spawn. Since plan 8R-1 a raid scope means raids only (no max battles), and the legacy `!wants` codec and the scope rules (`planSetWant`, `widerScope`) are unchanged.
+- What is no `PokemonNotification` is a `TargetWant` (plan 8R-1, `stop-reports.md`; table `TargetWant`, `ctx.targetWants`: `TargetWantStorage` `list`, `change`, `remove`, `removeAll`, `count`, `wanting(guildId, targets)` over the index `(guildId, target)`; twin `MemoryTargetWants`): a token per row (`src/domain/notify/target-wants.ts`: `research:pokemon:<dex>[:<form>]`, `research:item:<key>`, `research:energy:<dex>`, `dynamax:<dex>[:<form>]`, `gigantamax:<dex>[:<form>]`; 8R-2 adds the Rocket ones), written with an upsert that changes nothing (never `insert ignore`, which hides a foreign key's refusal). `/want target:` (no `type` since 8R-1; design 7, Matt's answers 2 and 9) takes a Pokémon, a form, a raid tier, perfect or zero IVs, or an item or Mega Energy of the task list (its autocomplete offers the Pokémon, forms, tiers and IVs first and the items and Mega Energy after them in what is left, at most five places (`REWARD_ROOM`) where the Pokémon would fill the list, `rewardWantChoices`; the design's "today's rewards first" is not built; `readWanted` reads typed text). It declares `defer` as a function: none where the dialog opens (the dialog is the first answer), `late` for every use that writes at once (the use's target is read once per interaction). A Pokémon or a form opens a dialog "Dratini: what for?" (`wantDialog`, one checkbox group `boxes`): Raids; Dynamax and Gigantamax where the game master or the max boss list has them; Spawns where it appears in the wild; Research but for a mega; Shadow where the game master has a shadow or a shadow raid boss of now is one (`pokemonBoxes`, `src/domain/pogo/want-boxes.ts`); a tier asks Raids and Shadow raids (`tierBoxes`). The boxes are ticked as the member's rows are (`WantBoxStorage.held`, read within the three seconds, `readInTime`); what can be only one thing (a mega, a tier without shadow raids), IVs and a reward are written at once. Raids and Spawns are the `PokemonNotification` row's scope, Shadow its shadow row, the others `TargetWant` rows: the Submit (`wantbox:p<dex>:set:<shown>[:<form>]`, `wantbox:t:set:<level>:<shown>`, `<shown>` the boxes the dialog showed as a bit per box of `allBoxes` in base 36, `wantBoxId`; `wantBoxControls`, `NOTIFICATION_THROTTLE`; a Submit without its checkbox group is `STALE_COMPONENT`) writes the boxes it showed, whatever can happen by then, in one transaction under the member's lock (`WantBoxStorage.set`, `planBoxes`; `WantBoxRepository`, twin `MemoryWantBoxes`); nothing ticked takes the target off. `/wants` lists each target once with its boxes ("Dratini: Raids, Research, Shadow"), and `/settings show` counts those lines (`wantLineCount`), `/unwant` takes every box of a target off, `/unwant-all` and the DM Stop buttons cover both tables.
 - What a member picked in the `target` option of `/want` or `/unwant` is a want token (`wantToken` / `parseWantToken`: `pokemon:<dex>[:<form>][:shadow]`, `tier:<level>[:shadow]`, `iv:perfect|zero`): the value of an autocomplete choice, never part of a custom id. Text sent without picking never guesses (`readWantText`): it acts only when it is a tier or IV word in full (`wantWord`), exactly a species' name (every form) or exactly one form's own name, with `shadow` before either; anything else is refused with suggestions. A bare number is a tier or IV word, never a Pokédex number.
 - Wants are named in one way everywhere (`wantLabel` / `wantName` in `src/commands/notifications/want-input.ts`): "X (every form)" for a species with several entries, "X (base form)" for its plain entry, "Shadow X", and the scope after " · " in the choices of `/unwant`.
 - Gym targets (`GymNotification`; `gym` holds a gym id as text) are `ctx.gymTargets` (`GymTargetStorage`), with `MemoryGymTargets` as the twin. In code "target" alone is what a want is for; a gym a member wants raids of is a gym target.

 ## The notifier
 
-- Whoever changes a party tells `PartyNotifier` (`src/services/notify-service.ts`) explicitly, with who acted: `maxReported` and `maxChanged` (plan 8X-3: a max battle's report, once its post exists, and a boss that is another; who wants the boss, `maxWantsFiring`: a species or form want in raids, never a tier, shadow or spawn want, no gym target; at most one DM an hour per member, boss and kind (a Gigantamax Machamp is told within the hour of a Dynamax one), `MAX_WANT_QUIET_MS`, kept in memory and lost on a restart, read when the members are gathered and written as each message is put in line, so two reports of one boss moments apart at two spots may both reach a member; the DM says so in small print, `maxHourNote`: "You won't be told about more Dynamax Machamp battles for an hour."; the spot's and the boss's names through `plainNoLinks`), `raidReported`, `raidChanged(before, after, actorId)` (the one call for every change of a raid; the notifier decides whether boss, tier or gym differ; the clock passes null), `raidMoving` / `raidMoved`, `trainCreated`, `meetingTimeChanged` (a group's meeting time in a raid or a max battle, `isBattle`; the DM names `the max battle at <spot>`), `startTimeChanged`, `spawnReported`. Every method returns at once and never throws (`safely`), and is called after the party's own effects. `NotifyService` matches with the pure functions of `src/domain/notify/reasons.ts`, asks `viewers`, and remembers per party which reasons it told which member: one DM per member and event, only for reasons not yet told, never to the actor (whose reasons count as told); the memory is shared by the two parties of a move across regions and forgotten at the party's end. A boss-set member is told every boss that differs from the last one they were told. Messages to everybody signed up (meeting and start times) have a line of their own per party, ask nobody and remember nothing. `close()` is for shutdown. Only meeting-time DMs are sent where `features.notifications` is off.
+- Whoever changes a party tells `PartyNotifier` (`src/services/notify-service.ts`) explicitly, with who acted: `maxReported` and `maxChanged` (plan 8X-3: a max battle's report, once its post exists, and a boss that is another; who wants the boss, `maxWantsFiring`: since plan 8R-1 the Dynamax box of a Dynamax battle and the Gigantamax box of a Gigantamax one (`TargetWant` `dynamax:` / `gigantamax:`, of the species or of the boss's form; Matt's answer 9 of the stop reports design), never a raid, tier, shadow or spawn want, no gym target; at most one DM an hour per member, boss and kind (a Gigantamax Machamp is told within the hour of a Dynamax one), `MAX_WANT_QUIET_MS`, kept in memory and lost on a restart, read when the members are gathered and written as each message is put in line, so two reports of one boss moments apart at two spots may both reach a member; the DM says so in small print, `maxHourNote`: "You won't be told about more Dynamax Machamp battles for an hour."; the spot's and the boss's names through `plainNoLinks`), `raidReported`, `raidChanged(before, after, actorId)` (the one call for every change of a raid; the notifier decides whether boss, tier or gym differ; the clock passes null), `raidMoving` / `raidMoved`, `trainCreated`, `meetingTimeChanged` (a group's meeting time in a raid or a max battle, `isBattle`; the DM names `the max battle at <spot>`), `startTimeChanged`, `spawnReported`, `researchReported` (plan 8R-1, `stop-reports.md`, "Wants and DMs": a research report's DM per region channel, with a member's own variant of the stops not told yet, `Announcement.variant`). Every method returns at once and never throws (`safely`), and is called after the party's own effects. `NotifyService` matches with the pure functions of `src/domain/notify/reasons.ts`, asks `viewers`, and remembers per party which reasons it told which member: one DM per member and event, only for reasons not yet told, never to the actor (whose reasons count as told); the memory is shared by the two parties of a move across regions and forgotten at the party's end. A boss-set member is told every boss that differs from the last one they were told. Messages to everybody signed up (meeting and start times) have a line of their own per party, ask nobody and remember nothing. `close()` is for shutdown. Only meeting-time DMs are sent where `features.notifications` is off.
 - New-train DMs are per member and server: `ctx.newTrains` (`NewTrainStorage`: `isOn`, `set`, `wanting(guildId)`; table `NewTrainNotification`; twin `MemoryNewTrains`). The legacy column `User.newTrain` is neither read nor written. Boss-set is still one setting of the member.
 
 ## Sending direct messages
 
-- Direct messages go out only through `DmSender` (`src/services/dm-sender.ts`; the app's is `QueuedDmSender`): `send(job)` puts a message in line and returns, never waits for Discord and never throws. A timer starts at most one send every 100 ms, five on their way at most; priorities are `DM_PRIORITY.urgent` (meeting times, boss-set), `spawn`, `normal` (raid wants, gym targets, new trains), the oldest event first within one; a job carries `eventAt` and `expiresAt` and is dropped once that has passed. There is no retry (discord.js waits out a 429), a pause of a minute when Discord refuses to open DM channels, an hour's memory of members who take no DMs, and a log line with the numbers of every burst. Never loop over recipients and send: the legacy bot lost its gateway connection that way. Tests use `RecordingDms` or `QueuedDmSender` over `FakeDmGateway` (`test/support/dms.ts`, `pullUntilIdle`). In rehearsal mode the members' sender is `RehearsalDms` over the queue: only the allowlist is written to (`operations.md`).
-- A DM of the notifier is a components-v2 message rendered by `src/render/notify-dm.ts` (`notifyDm`, the sentences, `stopHint`; plan 8B-1): one container, the news (its sentence first, for a phone's preview, without an address) with the party's brief and picture (`PartyBrief`, `spawnBrief`), a row of link buttons (`Go to post` by `postLink`, never `<#post>`; a raid's `Map`; `Go to report` for a spawn), then "You asked to be told about" and one section per reason with a `Stop` button beside it, as many as the message has room for beside its links and picture (`stopButtonRoom`; the rest are named in `stopHint`). `DmJob.message` is an `OutgoingMessage`. The meeting-time DM stays plain text. Their custom ids are `dm:<server>:stop:<what>` (`stopArgs` / `parseStopArgs`; documented in `custom-id.ts`; a want whose id would not fit gets no button and the DM names `/unwant`). The handler (`src/components/dm.ts`) removes the presser's own want or gym target in that server or switches the setting off, keeps nothing in memory, and shows the pressed button as a disabled `Stopped` (same custom id; `withStopped`) on a v2 DM, or takes it off (`withoutButton`) on a classic DM sent before 8B-1 (told apart by the message's `IsComponentsV2` flag).
+- Direct messages go out only through `DmSender` (`src/services/dm-sender.ts`; the app's is `QueuedDmSender`): `send(job)` puts a message in line and returns, never waits for Discord and never throws. There is no retry (discord.js waits out a 429), a pause of a minute when Discord refuses to open DM channels, an hour's memory of members who take no DMs, and a log line with the numbers of every burst. Never loop over recipients and send: the legacy bot lost its gateway connection that way. Tests use `RecordingDms` or `QueuedDmSender` over `FakeDmGateway` (`test/support/dms.ts`, `pullUntilIdle`). In rehearsal mode the members' sender is `RehearsalDms` over the queue: only the allowlist is written to (`operations.md`).
+- A DM of the notifier is a components-v2 message rendered by `src/render/notify-dm.ts` (`notifyDm`, the sentences, `stopHint`; plan 8B-1): one container, the news (its sentence first, for a phone's preview, without an address) with the party's brief and picture (`PartyBrief`, `spawnBrief`), a row of link buttons (`Go to post` by `postLink`, never `<#post>`; a raid's `Map`; `Go to report` for a spawn), then "You asked to be told about" and one section per reason with a `Stop` button beside it, as many as the message has room for beside its links and picture (`stopButtonRoom`; the rest are named in `stopHint`). `DmJob.message` is an `OutgoingMessage`. Their custom ids are `dm:<server>:stop:<what>` (`stopArgs` / `parseStopArgs`; documented in `custom-id.ts`; a `TargetWant` is `target` with `rp`, `ri`, `re`, `dx`, `gx` and a subject's every box `subject` with `sp` / `st`, plan 8R-1; a want whose id would not fit gets no button and the DM names `/unwant`). The handler (`src/components/dm.ts`) removes the presser's own want or gym target in that server or switches the setting off, keeps nothing in memory, and shows the pressed button as a disabled `Stopped` (same custom id; `withStopped`) on a v2 DM, or takes it off (`withoutButton`) on a classic DM sent before 8B-1 (told apart by the message's `IsComponentsV2` flag).
 - The owner's DM of a request for the Wayspot export tool (plan 8W-P; `web.md`, "The Wayspot export tool"): a new request, or one asked again after a refusal, queues a DM to `OWNER_ID` through `DmSender` (`normal`, expiring after 7 days; the queue is in memory, so a restart loses it and the page is the fallback), only while at most `OPEN_REQUESTS_NOTIFIED` 20 requests are open (any Discord account can ask; the rest wait on the page). It is `accessRequestDm` (`src/render/script-access-dm.ts`): who asks by name (`plainNoLinks`) and id as plain text, no mention, the community line through `plainNoLinks`, when, and **Approve** / **Refuse**, custom ids `scriptaccess:<row id>:approve|refuse:<askedAt in base 36>`. The handler (`scriptAccessControls`, `src/components/script-access.ts`) has a guard that the presser is `OWNER_ID` (a guard refusal counts against no throttle) and `SCRIPT_ACCESS_THROTTLE` 20 a minute; a press decides the request as it is now and for the asking it was drawn for, and edits the DM to what was decided and when without its buttons (`accessDecidedDm`): decided meanwhile, "Decided already: …"; asked again since, "Asked again since, <time>: decide it on its new DM or on the page."; a row gone or a button it cannot read is out of date. No fresh web login is needed for the DM.
 
 ## Spawn reports

index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..27292c0d690389bed0cb599b186171a15d0c166d

@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+# Reports at stops
+
+What members report at PokéStops (plan 8R-1; design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-stop-reports-design.md`): stops of Pine's own, the field research task list, research periods, the stop reports and `/research`, the pinned post "Today at the stops", and the research wants and their DMs. Team GO Rocket (plan 8R-2) adds a kind of report and a section of the post; the map (8R-3) a layer. Read before changing anything under `src/domain/stops/`, `src/domain/research/`, `src/commands/research/`, `src/commands/stops/`, or `src/services/` `stop-reports.ts`, `stop-posts.ts`, `research-task-service.ts`, `pine-stops.ts`.
+
+## The tables (migration 026)
+
+- One migration for all of 8R-1 (`2026_10_21_026_stop_reports.ts`), additive and guarded as the others: `PineStop` (a server's own stops: snowflake `serverId`, name, point, address, who made it, when), `StopReport` (one per server, stop key, kind and period: unique `(serverId, stopKey, kind, periodKey)`, `periodKey` up to 220 characters for the feed's longest event id and a day; the stop's snapshot, `subjectKey`, the detail as JSON, the reporter, `endsAt`, `madeAt`; the kind `research` now, `rocket` for 8R-2), `ResearchEvent` (the events of the feed with research: id, name, type, start, end, as last seen), `StopPost` (a region channel's post of a day: channel, local day, server, message ids in order), `TargetWant` (a member's want that is no `PokemonNotification`: server and member by their rows, the target token, unique on the three, indexed by server and token for the notifier) and `ResearchTask` (the last good task list: key, text, category, rewards as JSON, its place on the page, first and last seen, active).
+- Repositories and their twins (each pair runs one set of shared cases, `test/support/*-cases.ts`): `StopReportRepository` / `MemoryStopReports`, `PineStopRepository` / `MemoryPineStops`, `StopPostRepository` / `MemoryStopPosts`, `ResearchEventRepository` and `ResearchTaskRepository` / `test/support/research-store.ts`, `TargetWantRepository` / `MemoryTargetWants`, `WantBoxRepository` / `MemoryWantBoxes`.
+
+## Stops of Pine's own
+
+- A stop Wayfarer does not list (a sponsored one) is added by staff with `/pokestop add name: at: [address:]` (`src/commands/stops/pokestop.ts`, Manage Server and `requireBotManagement`, shaped like `/gym add`): `at` is a maps link, the game's share link or coordinates (`readLocation`), and must lie in a region of the server (`STOP_NOT_HERE`). Within `PINE_STOP_NEAR_METRES` (30) of a known stop (imported or Pine's own) it asks "Add anyway?" with the stops named (`pokestop:<token>:add|cancel`, `PendingRequests`, an hour); `/pokestop edit stop: [name:] [at:] [address:]` (`-` takes the address away) and `/pokestop remove stop:` (no dialog: a report keeps its snapshot) name a stop by the autocomplete of the server's own stops (`NO_SUCH_STOP` else).
+- `PineStopService` (`src/services/pine-stops.ts`, `ctx.pineStops`) keeps them in memory and hands them to `WayspotDirectory.setPineStops`: a Pine stop is a `Wayspot` of kind `stop` with `pineServer` set, keyed `pine-<id>` (`pineStopKey`, `pineStopIdOf`), placed only in the regions of its own server, so `PlaceFinder` (`/wild near:`, `/meetup` with meetup safety's checks, pin names, `/research`) finds it as any stop, and every change bumps the stop index's and the map's generation. `readPlaceValue` takes `stop:pine-<id>`; the region editor's cache leaves out other servers' Pine stops.
+- The Wayfarer import's preview names the Pine stops within 30 m of an imported stop (`pineStopsNear`), for staff to remove what Wayfarer lists now.
+
+## The task list
+
+- `settings.research` has a default for every key (always on, no switch): `url` (Leek Duck's `https://leekduck.com/research/`), `refreshHours` 1, `staleAfterHours` 6 (refused below twice `refreshHours`), `throttle` `{ uses: 10, minutes: 30 }`.
+- `ResearchTaskService` (`ctx.researchTasks`: `tasks()`, `byKey`, `readAt`) reads the page every `refreshHours` with Pine's User-Agent (`PINE_USER_AGENT`) and a byte cap (`readLimitedText`, `MAX_RESEARCH_PAGE_BYTES`), parses it (`parseResearchPage`, `src/domain/research/leekduck.ts`: tasks by category, rewards of `data-reward-type` `encounter` (a catalogue entry, shiny or not), `item` (key and quantity) and `resource` (Mega Energy of a species); the breakthrough is skipped), and keeps the last good list in `ResearchTask` so a start without the network still offers it. A read with fewer than half the tasks of the list in use is a warning and the list stays, unless the read before it listed the very same tasks or the list in use is older than `staleAfterHours` (then the page did shrink, and the smaller list is taken: a real shrink is never refused for good); a list not read for `staleAfterHours` is said once in the log. The kept list keeps the page's order. A task's key is `taskKeyOf` (an FNV-1a hash of `foldTaskText`), the value of its choice.
+- Whether the page shows an event's own tasks while the event runs is not known before 2026-11-09 (design 4.1): nothing reads event pages; a missing task is typed in full.
+
+## Research periods
+
+- The events feed's research flags (`extraData.generic.hasFieldResearchTasks`, `events.json` read where `events.min.json` lacks `extraData`) are kept as `ResearchEvent` rows by `RaidEventService` (`researchEvents()`, `ResearchEventProvider`), a stored event kept 30 days after its end, so a restart or an event dropped from the feed loses no period; one not begun that a read no longer lists (moved or cancelled) is dropped, as the raid events' (`removeNotSeen`); a read whose feed has no research flags at all (neither `events.min.json` nor `events.json`) keeps what is stored as it is, said once in the log. `onResearchChange(listener)` tells of every change (a read, the kept ones loaded): the pinned posts' timer and periods follow.
+- `src/domain/time/research-periods.ts` (pure): `periodAt(events, at, zone)` gives the period on (`day:<yyyy-mm-dd>` to local midnight; for a multi-day event, a rotation, `event:<id>:<yyyy-mm-dd>` per local day of it: its start and end rotate the tasks for good, and inside it the tasks roll over at each local midnight as on any day (Matt, 2026-10-22: Into the Wild's day 1 runs from 10:00 to midnight, its last day from midnight to 20:00, and the day's research after it is new); `event:<id>:<yyyy-mm-dd>` also for each day of a big event's hours, a window kept to the millisecond; an intra-day event is a window under which the day's reports wait and come back after it, `waiting`); `eventShape`: one local day is a `window`, a big event (`BIG_EVENT_TYPES`) over days whose hours end before midnight is `daily`, any other (crossing midnight included, Matt's answer 6) a `rotation`. `nextPeriodChange` is the next midnight, start or end. Midnight is Luxon's in `settings.timezone`, DST days included.
+
+## Reports and `/research`
+
+- `StopReportService` (`ctx.stopReports`) reports a task at one to five stops in the period on now (`reportResearch`): each stop's report of the period is replaced, whoever made it (`StopReportStorage.save` gives the one replaced), and ends with the period (`endsAt`). Listeners hear `changed(serverId)` (the posts) and `reported(news)` (the notifier: only stops that did not have this very task in the period). A replacement is a report of its own: the replaced row is deleted and a new one made under the same lock, so a report's id never changes what it is (an old answer's Take back or "Same task at more stops…" finds its report gone and answers so; `/research remove` takes back by the id it read, and says `REPORT_CHANGED` where the report was replaced meanwhile). `takeBack(serverId, ids, by, staff)` removes a member's own reports, any for staff; a replaced report does not come back. The hourly upkeep (`PartyScheduler`, `stops`) sweeps ended reports.
+- `/research report task: stop: [stop2: … stop5:] [reward:]` and `/research remove stop:` (`src/commands/research/`): from a region's channel, forum or post (`RESEARCH_FROM_A_REGION`); where the server's regions hold no stop, `NO_STOPS_HERE` (Matt's answer 7). `task` is a choice of the list (found by reward words too) or text typed in full (free text, capped at 100 characters, shown through `plainNoLinks`; with `reward:` a Pokémon, item or Mega Energy); a key gone from the list is `TASK_LIST_CHANGED`. A stop is a choice of the stops (`stop:<key>`), typed text naming one, or a maps link (the nearest stop within 50 m, `PlaceFinder.nearestStop`). The guard reads all of it so a refusal does not count; the throttle is `settings.research.throttle` in a window of its own (`researchThrottle`, `researchWindow`); one report of five stops counts once. `defer: 'late'`.
+- The answer (`researchAnswer`, `src/render/research.ts`, for the reporter alone): the task and rewards, each stop (with what it replaced, "again" for the same task), where it shows (in rehearsal mode, which makes no post, only until when) and until when (`periodEndWords`: "until midnight", the time, with its day when it is not today), "Same task at more stops…" (`research:<id>:more`: a menu of up to 25 stops within `MORE_STOPS_METRES` (2 km) of the first without this task in the period, five at once; it counts in `/research report`'s window through the throttle's `as`, gives the use back where the report has ended or was replaced (`REPORT_ENDED`, `givesBack`), and answers apart with its own Take back) and "Take back" (`research:<id>:back[:<id>…]`, as many ids as fit; the rest by `/research remove`).
+
+## The pinned post "Today at the stops"
+
+- `StopPostService` (`src/services/stop-posts.ts`): one post per region channel and local day, made at the first report of the day in the region, pinned (the "pinned a message" notice deleted where the bot may; at Discord's pin limit, or without Pin Messages, it stands unpinned and that is logged once per channel), drawn anew `POST_DELAY_MS` (3 s) after the last change (`Gathered`, coalesced) in one queue per channel (`KeyedLock`), the midnight delete included; reads are done before any Discord call. A timer at `nextPeriodChange` draws every kept post anew (`draw` deletes the post of an ended day and makes today's where reports stand); `start()` does the same for what a restart left (`StopPost` keeps the ids, each message's saved as soon as it is sent, before it is pinned), and sets the timer also when the kept posts cannot be read; a change of the research events (`onResearchChange`) draws the posts anew and sets the timer again (those redraws in a set of their own, which `flush` and `close` wait for and `messageOf` does not: it waits only for its own channel). It is kept, saying "Nothing reported right now.", when every report is taken back. None in rehearsal mode.
+- `stopPostMessages` (`src/render/stop-post.ts`): research grouped by task, most stops first, each with its rewards and up to 15 stops (`- **Stop** · address · **Reporter**`, whole lines only, as many as fit, the rest counted: "…and N more stops"), the reward's picture beside it; within 40 components and `TEXT_BUDGET` a message, spilling into a second and third (`MAX_POST_MESSAGES`), then "…and N more tasks"; under an event the event's line (its tasks `until …` as `periodEndWords` says it), under an intra-day window when the day's research comes back. Where the bot may not embed, plain text of 2,000 characters a message (`stopPostText`). Both give the layout's `placement` (which message holds each task), so `messageOf(channelId, subjectKey)` (the channel's waiting change drawn first, `Gathered.flushKey`) gives a DM its link. 8R-2's hideouts go after the research.
+- `PartyGateway.pinMessage` / `unpinMessage` (`PinOutcome`: `pinned`, `full`, `not-allowed`, `gone`); Pin Messages is optional in `REGION_CHANNEL_NEEDS`, so `cutover-check` warns where it lacks.
+
+## Wants and DMs
+
+- `/want`'s dialog, `TargetWant` and the matching are in `notifications-and-dms.md` ("Wants and gym targets", "The notifier").
+- A report that is news (`StopReportService`'s `reported`) goes to `NotifyService.researchReported`: who wants a reward of its task (`researchTargets` / `researchWantsFiring`, `src/domain/notify/reasons.ts`: a Pokémon's Research box, the species fitting any form, an item whatever the quantity, a species' Mega Energy) is told at the normal priority, one DM per report and region channel naming that region's stops with their addresses (`researchDmSentence`, `researchDmBrief`: "Field research has been reported in #region by **Name**: **task**.", the rewards, the stops, until when as `periodEndWords` says it; all through `plainNoLinks`), only members who can view the channel, never the reporter, only under `features.notifications`, expiring with the report, with "Go to post" to the message of the pinned post holding the task (`researchPosts`; none in rehearsal mode). A member told of a task at a stop in a period is not told again (`researchTold`, in memory: a restart can repeat one), so a later "Same task at more stops…" names only the new stops. The usual Stop buttons (`target` reasons, `stopArgs` `rp`/`ri`/`re`).

 - Wayfarer tests: the import and the queue over gym administration on fakes are `wayfarerImportWith()` (`test/support/wayfarer-import.ts`: `wayfarer`, `wayfarerReview`, `wayfarerStore`, `wayspotStore` (`MemoryWayspots`) and `wayspots` (a `WayspotDirectory` over it, loaded), `admin`, `directory`, `removal`), which `gymCommandsWith()` routes like the bot; `createTestContext`'s own `wayfarer` and `wayfarerReview` throw when used. Exports in tests are built from invented Wayspots at the invented gyms, their cells by `wayfarerCellAt`. Kept Wayspots: `MemoryWayspots` keeps those found gone apart (`goneRows`, plan 8W-3); `keptRow(n, overrides)` and `wayspotId(n)` (`test/support/wayspot-cases.ts`, with `wayspotCases`, which the repository and `MemoryWayspots` both run), `wayspotsWith(rows)` (a loaded directory over the invented regions; pass it as `wayspots` to `createTestContext`, whose own is empty, `noWayspots()`, and whose `placeFinder` is built over its own gyms, Wayspots and regions unless given; a test that searches stops or power spots awaits `placeFinder.built()` first, as the search indexes are built in a turn of their own). Never the real export: it is read only by scratch scripts.
 
+## Reports at stops (plan 8R-1)
+
+- Each repository of `stop-reports.md` and its twin run one set of cases: `stopReportCases` (`test/support/stop-report-cases.ts`, with `reportedStop(n, overrides)` (Yellow Mural `n` at 40.44…, −79.99: outside the invented regions, so a test that needs a region moves it, as `west(n)` in `stop-posts.test.ts`), `researchReport()`, `REPORT_NOW`, `REPORT_SERVER`, `DRATINI`), `pineStopCases` (`newPineStop()`), `researchEventCases`, `researchTaskCases` and `stopPostCases` (`test/support/research-store-cases.ts`, with `INTO_THE_WILD`, `PAWNIARD_DAY`, `listedTask()`; twins `MemoryResearchEvents`, `MemoryResearchTasks`, `MemoryStopPosts` in `test/support/research-store.ts`), `targetWantCases` (its constants of every kind of target), `wantBoxCases`.
+- The task list: `readResearchPage()` (Leek Duck's page of 2026-10-21, `test/fixtures/leekduck-research.html`, unchanged: 58 tasks, 299 rewards), `researchTasksOfPage()` (parsed once, frozen), `pageTask(text)` and `researchTasksFixture(tasks?, readAt?)` (`test/support/research.ts`, a `ResearchTaskProvider`, `ctx.researchTasks` of `createTestContext()`). Research events: `raidEventsFixture(zone, { research })`; the events feed fixture `test/fixtures/max-events.json` holds the two research events of November 2026.
+- `createTestContext()` gives `ctx.stopReports` (a `StopReportService` over `MemoryStopReports` and the context's events), `ctx.pineStops` (none, over memory and the context's Wayspots), `ctx.targetWants` and `ctx.wantBoxes` (`MemoryWantBoxes` over the context's wants and target wants); `partyServiceWith()` gives `targetWants` to the notifier (`made.targetWants`), and `notifying.researchPosts` a test's own links (`notify-service.research.test.ts`).
+- `FakePartyGateway` pins (`pinMessage` / `unpinMessage`): `noPinning` (channels where it is `not-allowed`), `pinLimit`, `pinNotices` (the notices it deleted), `pinnedIn(channelId)`.
+
 ## The Wayspot export tool (plan 8W-P)
 
 - The package's contracts: `@pine/wayspot-core/fixtures/export-v1.json` (and `.json.gz`) and `import-report.csv` are pinned byte for byte (`.gitattributes`: never converted); `export-contract.test.ts` in the package reads and writes the export, `src/render/wayfarer-report.contract.test.ts` checks the report writer still makes the CSV (`importReportFixtureText`, `test/support/import-report-fixture.ts`) and that its `gym` and `cell` columns are there. A fixture made anew is checked against the tool first (`fixtures/README.md`).

 ## The kept Wayspots
 
 - Every Wayspot of an applied import is kept (plan 8W-2): table `Wayspot` (migration `2026_10_16_017_wayspot`; a migration merged after it must sort after it, since Kysely refuses an earlier name once 017 ran on a database: 8H's is `2026_10_16_018_party_history`, 016 stays unused; first merge wins, the second renumbers above it, and only a merged migration, or one that already sorts after everything merged, is run on the dev database. The table: the Wayfarer id, `kind`, `formerKind` (the kind before an import last saw it as another; `stop` for a promoted stop), place, title and address plain (not entity-encoded: nothing legacy reads it; cut to 255), picture (`pictureOf`, the address as Wayfarer gives it; a message shows it through `wayspotPicture`: https, `=s400`), `firstSeen` (when an import first kept it: the import's time), `lastSeen` (when the scan of the newest file that saw it was made, `scanTimeOf`: the file's `finishedAt`, else `startedAt`, else the import's time, never later than the import's time: a file dated in the future would freeze its rows); not per server) behind `WayspotStorage` (`WayspotRepository`: `all`, `gone`, `saveFromImport({ upsert, remove, gone }, importedAt, scannedAt, startedAt)` in one transaction of chunks of 500, `remove(ids)`; twin `MemoryWayspots`, both run `wayspotCases`). The pure part is `planKept` (`src/domain/wayspots/keep.ts`, rows `kept.ts`): every Wayspot of the file but those whose id is a Pine gym's `pogoId` (of any server) after the import, which live in `Gym` (a row of one is deleted); a kept row not in the file is marked gone where the file covered its cell (`coveredCells`; plan 8W-3: the row stays with `kind` `gone`, its kind before in `formerKind` and its `lastSeen` the time of the scan that found it gone, never read by `all`; no column was added, ruling: tombstones are kept for good, a few thousand rows at most: nothing prunes them, and every preview and import reads them all, `WayspotStorage.gone`, with the kind each had, `GoneWayspot` (a stop where it is not known, `UNKNOWN_GONE_KIND`, so that no tombstone is left out); one brought back keeps that kind as its `formerKind`, and a Wayfarer gym added that was such a stop counts as one, `promoted`), and a Wayspot a newer scan found gone (`KeptInput.gone`, from `WayspotStorage.gone`) is not brought back by an older file (a newer one brings it back, keeping its `firstSeen`); the storage keeps these guards itself whatever the caller planned (plan 8W-3: an upsert never overwrites a row, kept or gone, last seen after the file's scan, by MySQL's row alias `AS new` with `IF(Wayspot.lastSeen > new.lastSeen, …)`, `lastSeen` assigned last; a row is marked gone only when not seen since the file's scan started, or at its own scan time), so that imports that were not one after the other cannot undo each other either; a row last seen after the file's scan (another server's newer scan) is neither changed nor deleted nor counted (a week-old file does not undo a fresh scan; only a gym that is it now takes it), and one another scan saw after the file's scan started (`scanStartOf`: `startedAt`, else `finishedAt`, never later than the import) is not deleted (a row last seen exactly at the file's scan time is its own: an earlier import of the same scan); moves and renames are silent; `WayspotCounts` counts stops and power spots `added`, `changed` (kind, title, place, address or picture), `gone` (also a stop that became a gym), and `gyms` (kept Wayfarer gyms written, said nowhere and no reason to offer an import). The import reads the kept rows under its lock, writes them after the gyms (`Unrecorded` `wayspots` when it fails or they cannot be read; the gyms stand, and a gym added is then not known to have been a PokéStop) and stores the counts in its row as `wayspots*`; preview and outcome say them in one line (a preview that cannot read them logs it and says nothing of them), and an import that changes only stops and power spots is offered (`changesNothing`, `changesWayspots`). A Wayfarer gym whose adding failed stays a kept `gym` row. A review's Same as (`applyMatch`) and New gym delete the row of the Wayspot the gym now is; New gym gives the gym the kept row's picture. A Wayfarer gym added whose kept row was a stop (`wasStop`) is counted by `GymBatch.add(…, { promoted: true })`: the summary says "Professor Pine has added 12 gyms (3 of them were PokéStops)". The summary also says what the import changed of the stops and power spots (`planKept`'s `byKind`, `WayspotChanges`, given to the batch by `GymBatch.countWayspots` once they are written), each count by its kind: "It also added 120 PokéStops and 3 power spots, changed 4 PokéStops, and removed 2 power spots."; its `gone` is only what left Wayfarer's map, not a stop that became a gym (unlike `WayspotCounts.gone`, which the preview says): a stop Wayfarer now shows as a gym, taken by a Pine gym or not, is counted neither as removed nor as a stop. Its `changed` is only a new kind, a new title or a move over `NOTICED_MOVE_METRES` 10 (`noticeable`): a new address or picture alone is written but not said, so that routine re-imports post nothing (the preview's `changed` still counts them). Real export (43,057): `planKept` 0.2 s, the first write 1.9 s, a write of all again 1.2 s.
-- `ctx.wayspots` is `WayspotDirectory` (`src/services/wayspot-directory.ts`): loaded at start (after the regions) and after every applied import, empty until then; `byId`, `all`, `inRegion(channelId)`, `regionsOf(id)` (by the outlines, worked out again when `RegionDirectory.generation` changes), `near(point, metres, kinds?)`, `forget(ids)` (an id forgotten while a load reads stays forgotten when the load ends), a `generation` that changes with every load, forget and change of the regions (the region editor of 8M-2 rebuilds on it), and a `contentGeneration` that changes only with what the Wayspots are (every load; not the regions, not a forget: what is built of them passes over a forgotten one through `inRegion` and `byId`), with `whenChanged(listener)` called after each change of it (the search indexes of `PlaceFinder` are built on it, and `PartyService` shows the meetups near a PokéStop or power spot anew, plan 8D). `near` also names a pin: `PlaceFinder.pin` takes the nearest gym of the server or kept PokéStop or power spot within 50 m.
+- `ctx.wayspots` is `WayspotDirectory` (`src/services/wayspot-directory.ts`): loaded at start (after the regions) and after every applied import, empty until then; it also holds the stops of Pine's own (plan 8R-1, `setPineStops` from `PineStopService`: kind `stop`, `pineServer` set, keyed `pine-<id>`, in the regions of their own server only; each change bumps both generations; `stop-reports.md`); `byId`, `all`, `inRegion(channelId)`, `regionsOf(id)` (by the outlines, worked out again when `RegionDirectory.generation` changes), `near(point, metres, kinds?)`, `forget(ids)` (an id forgotten while a load reads stays forgotten when the load ends), a `generation` that changes with every load, forget and change of the regions (the region editor of 8M-2 rebuilds on it), and a `contentGeneration` that changes only with what the Wayspots are (every load; not the regions, not a forget: what is built of them passes over a forgotten one through `inRegion` and `byId`), with `whenChanged(listener)` called after each change of it (the search indexes of `PlaceFinder` are built on it, and `PartyService` shows the meetups near a PokéStop or power spot anew, plan 8D). `near` also names a pin: `PlaceFinder.pin` takes the nearest gym of the server or kept PokéStop or power spot within 50 m.

 ## 6. Gyms
 
 - **One at a time:** `/gym add` with the link Pokémon GO shares for the gym (or its coordinates) and its name. `/gym edit`, `/gym move` and `/gym delete` change it later.
+- **PokéStops Wayfarer does not list** (sponsored ones): `/pokestop add` with its name and the link Pokémon GO shares for it (or a maps link, or its coordinates); `/pokestop edit` and `/pokestop remove` change it later. Members find it wherever a PokéStop is asked for.
 - **All at once, from Wayfarer:** `/gym import` reads an export of the gyms, PokéStops and power spots Wayfarer has. The export is made by the Pine Wayspot export tool: ask for it at https://profpine.com/userscript (your settings' `wayspotTool`, which `/help gym` names). It takes the KML file of `/region export`. Then attach the file it saves to `/gym import`: it shows what it would do first, and what needs a person goes to `/gym review`. `/help gym` has the details, and [wayfarer.md](../architecture/wayfarer.md) the whole design.
 
 ## 7. Forums
 
 Once regions and gyms are in, a staff member runs `/admin setup-forums` in your server: every region gets a forum beside its channel (named after the channel with `-meetups`, the `regionForumSuffix` setting), its tags, and a pinned list of active raids. It changes nothing that is already there but for taking off tags the bot no longer uses (such as EX), so it is safe to run again; a region that fails says why (most often the category's permissions for the bot).
 
-Then try it: `/raid` in a region channel, the buttons in the post, `/max` (a max battle at a power spot: the power spots come with the Wayfarer import), `/train`, `/meetup`, `/want` and a report of that boss by somebody else. `/help` lists everything.
+Then try it: `/raid` in a region channel, the buttons in the post, `/max` (a max battle at a power spot: the power spots come with the Wayfarer import), `/train`, `/meetup`, `/research report` (the task of a PokéStop: the region's pinned post "Today at the stops" shows it), `/want` and a report of that boss by somebody else. `/help` lists everything.

+
+Prototype on `proto-8r1` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/stop-reports/var/proto-8r1`), eight tasks and the docs; area file `docs/architecture/stop-reports.md`.
+
+- **Watch Leek Duck's research page on 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-21:** whether `https://leekduck.com/research/` lists an event's own tasks while it runs (Into the Wild from 2026-11-09 10:00; Pawniard Community Day 2026-11-21 14:00–17:00). Nothing reads event pages; a task missing from the list is typed in full. If the page keeps the ordinary tasks during an event, 8R-1 needs the event's page or a staff list.
+- **Research periods (Matt, 2026-10-22):** a multi-day research event that is no big event (Into the Wild, 10:00 to 20:00 over five days, or one crossing midnight) rotates the tasks at its start and end for good, and inside it the tasks roll over at each local midnight: a period per day, `event:<id>:<date>`. Big events keep their daily windows (event tasks in their hours, the day's research before and after, coming back). Design 4.2 and answer 6 to be updated by the controller.
+- **`/want`'s autocomplete** offers the Pokémon, forms, tiers and IVs first and the items and Mega Energy after them, at most five places of a full list (fix rounds 1 and 2, B5); the design's "today's encounter rewards first" is not built.
+- **`/settings show`** counts the lines of `/wants`, both tables (fix round 1); one more read for it (6 statements).
+- **Research DMs** remember in memory who was told of a task at a stop in its period (as max battles' quiet hour): a restart can repeat one. A report whose stops lie in two regions with posts of their own sends one DM per region channel, each with its post's link; a stop in both regions is named once.
+- **A DM's link** draws its channel's post at once (`StopPostService.messageOf`, `Gathered.flushKey`): that channel skips the three seconds of gathering when somebody wants the task.
+- **The announcement drafts** (`2026-10-16-phase-8l2-announcements.md`): Pittsburgh's post is at Discord's 2,000 characters and does not name `/research` (a swap for Matt: one line out for it); the official post's first message was already 2,176 characters before 8R-1 (2,348 now): split it or trim before it is posted.
